name: Dual-Operator Constraint-First MOND (DOC-MOND)
claimed_mechanism: We introduce two algebraic auxiliary scalars: chi (the standard Legendre MOND scalar) and s (a frame-screw potential). The MOND force law is enforced exactly by a spatially nonlocal constraint D_i[mu(D^i chi)] = rho, using the frozen F+ primitive. The second scalar s is constrained to couple to the 3-acceleration a_mu via a coefficient strictly proportional to 1-mu(y)=e^-y. Because s is purely algebraic (kinetic: none), it generates the necessary DC-013 off-ray lensing slip without carrying its own kinetic normalization, completely bypassing the P7 strong-coupling wall that kills propagating preferred-frame fields.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the spatial nonlocal constraint generates the MOND potential (dynamics and lensing track each other exactly, eta=1). The screened frame-screw s = e^-y * (local acceleration functional) introduces a subleading correction to the spatial metric perturbation Psi, breaking the diff-invariance slip-lock. Because s is screened by e^-y, the PPN preferred-frame parameters alpha_1 and alpha_2 vanish exponentially in the Solar System, satisfying G7 without requiring any propagating vector DOF.
inequivalence_argument: This architecture is strictly inequivalent to DC-010/DC-014 (which require a propagating khronon or vector with a kinetic term, triggering P7) and DC-012 (which lacks a preferred frame, failing the slip-lock). By making the frame-screw field s strictly auxiliary (zero kinetic term, algebraically slaved to the metric), we provide the required off-ray slip for correct MOND lensing (DC-013 escape) while ensuring that no propagating preferred-frame mode exists to develop a diverging or vanishing kinetic normalization (P7 escape). The MOND nonlocality is applied to the primary force carrier chi, while the frame-screw s is local, resolving the algebraic mismatch observed in FM-000010.
